claims.text: The target alloy has an interpenetrating, multiphase eutectic microstructure containing compositionally distinct phases and interphase boundaries.
Interphase boundaries are zones of weakened oxide-film adhesion.
Interphase boundaries are zones of local galvanic activity.
An incipient protective oxide film forms on the HEA surface at elevated temperature.
Mechanical wear removes or damages nascent protective oxide layers.
Wear preferentially removes or damages oxide at interphase boundaries.
Oxide removal exposes fresh, compositionally diverse substrate regions.
Compositional differences between the eutectic phases create galvanic couples.
Freshly exposed phase regions rapidly re-oxidize and undergo localized corrosion because of galvanic differences.
Repeated oxide removal, fresh-metal exposure, corrosion, and oxide reformation perpetuate a cyclic degradation mechanism.
The oxide-removal and reformation cycle is more rapid and severe under simultaneous wear and corrosion than under either isolated condition.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion will produce significantly greater total degradation than a matched wear-only or corrosion-only test.
Wear damage will be exacerbated during simultaneous exposure because oxide protection is impaired.
Corrosion rate will be higher during simultaneous exposure because wear continuously exposes reactive surfaces and enables localized galvanic effects.
Elevated temperature accelerates oxidation kinetics in the proposed corrosive environment.
The proposed mechanism applies when wear is intense enough to continuously disrupt the surface oxide.
Wear-only, corrosion-only, and simultaneous tests on identically prepared specimens provide the proposed controlled comparison.
The synergy criterion is that simultaneous total degradation exceeds the sum of the wear-only and corrosion-only effects.
Intact oxide films under mechanical action would falsify oxide-film removal as the driver of accelerated degradation.

contradictions.description: The prediction and baseline compare simultaneous degradation with either isolated test individually, whereas the falsification rule uses the stricter comparison with the sum of wear-only and corrosion-only losses. Thus the stated prediction could be satisfied while the stated synergy/falsification criterion is not.
